discovery: Quantum control of macroscopic mechanical oscillators: ground-state preparation and quantum coherent manipulation of engineered mechanical motion

nominees.name: Andrew N. Cleland
nominees.affiliation: Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering, University of Chicago, USA

nominees.name: Markus Aspelmeyer
nominees.affiliation: University of Vienna and IQOQI Vienna, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Quantum optics / quantum optomechanics and macroscopic quantum physics
motivation: For decades, mechanical motion of human-made objects was considered irreducibly classical. The nominees overturned this view. Cleland (2010) placed a micromechanical resonator in its quantum ground state and swapped single quanta between it and a superconducting qubit, the first quantum control of an engineered mechanical object. Painter (2011) used radiation pressure alone to laser-cool a nanomechanical optomechanical crystal to its ground state, and with Aspelmeyer demonstrated nonclassical phonon-photon correlations. Aspelmeyer pioneered radiation-pressure cooling, strong optomechanical coupling and, recently, ground-state cooling of levitated nanoparticles, opening tests of quantum mechanics with massive objects and gravity. Together these advances established mechanical oscillators alongside atoms, ions and superconducting circuits as quantum systems, enabling measurements at the standard quantum limit, quantum transduction between microwave and optical photons, and new sensors. They naturally extend the macroscopic quantum phenomena recognized in 2025.
